summary: The starter prompt clearly defines a Python LlamaIndex RAG agent that uses Azure DocumentDB as a vector store and must return the top-5 similar resolutions injected as context. Many low-level choices (Python version, exact embedding & chat models, collection schema, API surface, seed scripts, infra-as-code, test strategy, pinned deps, README details, index tuning) are not specified and will be chosen by the builder or filled by installed skills (notably documentdb-vector-search, documentdb-driver and documentdb-connection).

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python LlamaIndex RAG agent that indexes past ticket resolutions and knowledge base articles in a DocumentDB vector store... retrieve the top 5 similar past resolutions... generate a suggested resolution"
rubric.note: Business problem, user (support agent) and what to demonstrate (RAG over DocumentDB) are explicit.
Single-agent RAG, using LlamaIndex is explicit.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use Python 3.11 (virtualenv via python/pip as provided in run environment).
rubric.note: The prompt states Python but not a version. The supplied run-environment notes say python/pip are available but don't name a version; builder will pick a modern 3.10/3.11 runtime (I assume 3.11).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use PyMongo (pymongo>=4.9) and follow the singleton MongoClient pattern; prefer AsyncMongoClient if implementing async code.
rubric.note: Installed skills give driver best-practices (singleton client, connection reuse) and connection guidance (TLS, SCRAM-SHA-256). The prompt didn't pick a driver or version; the builder will follow those skills' recommendations.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the provided vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol) as described in the run environment.
rubric.note: The sample's skill_md explicitly states a reachable M30 vector-capable cluster is available and must be used.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment; TLS required and SCRAM-SHA-256 as auth mechanism; provide a .env.example with placeholders and never commit secrets.
rubric.note: Run environment instructs the connection string is in DOCUMENTDB_URI and to not write it into files. documentdb-connection documents TLS/auth expectations.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "indexes past ticket resolutions and knowledge base articles... each stored as a document carrying its own embedding"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a single collection (e.g., `documents` or `kb_documents`) with documents: {_id, type: 'kb'|'resolution', title, content, embedding: [float], metadata: {...}, created_at}. No sharding for the sample.
rubric.note: Prompt requires storing docs with embeddings but leaves collection names and exact fields unspecified. documentdb-data-modeling skill provides patterns but not the exact schema; builder will pick a simple document shape as assumed above.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a small synthetic seed dataset (~50–200 docs: mix of KB articles and resolved tickets) bundled in a `seed/` folder and a `seed.py` idempotent script that inserts/upserts documents.
rubric.note: The prompt expects indexing of past resolutions and KB articles but does not specify data source, size, license, or a seed script. Local-deployment skill has best-practice guidance but not the actual seed data.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "indexes ... in a DocumentDB vector store" and "retrieve the top 5 similar past resolutions"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a cosmosSearch vector index (choose `vector-diskann` for an M30 cluster) on an `embedding` field with `dimensions` equal to the embedding model's output; query via $search/cosmosSearch returning top-k=5 and include similarity score in results.
rubric.note: The prompt requests vector search/top-5. documentdb-vector-search prescribes index types and query patterns; exact index parameters and dimensions are not in the prompt and must match the chosen embedding model (see risks).

rubric.found_in_prompt: "LlamaIndex RAG agent" (implies embedding and LLM use) but no model/provider specified
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use OpenAI (or another configured provider) for embeddings and LLM calls. Example defaults: embeddings = text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims) and chat/generation = gpt-4o-mini or gpt-4o. Expose model/provider credentials via environment variables (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY).
rubric.note: The prompt does not name embedding model/dimensions or generation model/provider. These are critical because index dimensions and similarity choices must match the embedding model.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "When a new ticket arrives... generate a suggested resolution"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement a minimal Flask HTTP API with POST /suggest (JSON {"ticket_text": ...}) that returns {suggested_resolution, sources:[...], scores:[...]}. Also include a CLI helper script (e.g., `tools/submit_ticket.py`).
rubric.note: The prompt expects end-to-end handling of an incoming ticket but doesn't mandate CLI vs API vs UI. Builder will pick an API + CLI for a sample.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision a new cluster for the sample; use the existing cluster in the run environment. If infra-as-code is provided, it would use the Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource via Bicep but the prompt does not request this.
rubric.note: The run environment states a cluster already exists. The prompt doesn't ask for infrastructure code; a gallery sample often requires it but this starter prompt omits that requirement.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include README with steps: create virtualenv, pip install -r requirements.txt, copy .env.example to .env, run `python seed.py`, run `python app.py`, then POST to /suggest. Provide example curl requests and expected output.
rubric.note: Prompt does not include concrete commands or what constitutes a successful run; the builder will add these standard instructions.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Definition of done: code runs locally against the provided cluster, seed script populates documents, /suggest returns a suggestion built from top-5 retrieved docs, README documents steps, and no secrets are committed.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria in the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep costs low by using the existing cluster; do not provision extra clusters. Sample should not target production HA or CMK. No PII beyond synthetic examples.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't set cost/scale constraints or compliance limits.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a conventional layout: README.md, requirements.txt (pinned), src/, seed.py, app.py, tests/ with unit tests, .env.example, LICENSE, and an explanation that the sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB".
rubric.note: Conventions are not specified; builder will pick typical layout and naming for gallery samples.

questions_for_author: Which embedding model and provider should the sample use (e.g., OpenAI text-embedding-3-small with 1536 dims)? the embedding model choice determines index dimensions and must be fixed.
Which generation/chat model and provider should the agent call for suggestion generation (e.g., OpenAI gpt-4o-mini)?
Do you want an HTTP API (e.g., Flask/FastAPI) with a POST /suggest endpoint, or is a CLI/demo script sufficient?
Should the sample include infrastructure-as-code (Bicep/Terraform) to provision an Azure DocumentDB cluster, or must it only use the existing cluster noted in the run environment?
Do you require unit tests that run without a live cluster (mocks/fakes)? If so, prefer pytest with fixture mocks for the DocumentDB client and embedding calls.
requirements_at_risk: The vector index dimensions must match the embedding model's output — embedding model is not specified in the prompt, so builder may choose a model and could set dimensions incorrectly.

The vector index parameters (lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree, subtype) tuned for the sample's data size and README guidance on scaling — prompt doesn't ask for index parameter choices or guidance for larger data sets.
A `.env.example` listing every required setting with placeholders — prompt doesn't request it explicitly (though skill_md recommends it).
A seed script that loads sample data idempotently (can be run twice without duplicating) — prompt asks to index past resolutions but doesn't mandate an idempotent seed script.
Search results include similarity score — prompt asks for top-5 retrieval but not that results include returned similarity scores.
/search (or equivalent) returns clear errors for empty queries and when embedding calls fail — prompt doesn't require or specify error handling contract for empty input or embedding failures.
Dependencies pinned in `requirements.txt` — prompt does not specify dependency pinning.
Unit tests that run without a live cluster (using mocks) — prompt doesn't demand test coverage or mocking strategy.

Infrastructure for the cluster provided as code (Azure DocumentDB resource) — prompt does not request infra-as-code; run environment already provides a cluster but the gallery reference wants infra code.
README must cover what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — prompt does not explicitly require a complete README, though this is expected for gallery samples.

Context-engineering details that explicitly trim retrieved resolutions to relevant passages before injection — prompt requests concise/focused prompts but does not specify an algorithm (passage-splitting, scoring & trimming) so implementation may vary and may not match the reference expectation exactly.
